doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Bringing listeners back with Pharoah Sanders
summary: He used fingers and elbows for bigger sounds, and urged Pharoah to bring listeners back from the free sections.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Some of the things you did with Pharoah Sanders, the music would be going along sort of peaceful, and then something would happen.

That’s a good point. That was the thing I really brought to Pharoah. Because I said well you know we’d be playing and we’d just keep on exploring. And I remember I had ten fingers and I said wait a minute — and Pharoah was getting all these sounds, I said I need more sounds. So I used my fingers and then I used my elbows, you know, to get a bigger sound. And, but it was all musical, we wasn’t banging or nothing, but so I told Pharoah, I said, Pharoah, we can’t leave the people out there. We’ve got to bring them back. So we’d be playing then all of a sudden then we’d come on back to what they’re used to. [plays] You know so I always told Pharoah, I said Pharoah we’ve got to bring them back the way we started. And it worked.
Because you can leave them out there, like you say, it got strange.
